Recent work supports combining local sequence modeling with global temporal transitions. TGCL4SR (AAAI 2024) builds a temporal item-transition graph from interaction histories and adds time-interval embeddings to a Transformer; TagRec (TKDE 2025) combines temporal collaborative patterns with graph augmentation to address sparsity. These offer mechanisms compatible with histories and timestamps, without requiring pretrained text representations. [TGCL4SR](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28789), [TagRec](https://doi.org/10.1109/TKDE.2025.3538706).

Complementarity needs more than similarity: SComGNN (AAAI 2024) models both relevance and dissimilarity using low-pass and mid-pass graph filters. However, observed next-item transitions do not establish complementarity. SCRM explicitly constructs substitute/complement graphs using distinct click and purchase behaviors—supervision unavailable here. Likewise, ST2SI (COLING 2025) learns text-to-ID transition patterns through LLM tuning, so its pretrained component cannot transfer under these constraints. [SComGNN](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28734), [SCRM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.14957), [ST2SI](https://aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.171/).

Practical hypothesis, rather than a published result for this benchmark: augment SASRec with a smoothed directed transition score and asymmetric text compatibility, x_iᵀWx_j, using TF-IDF or training-corpus SVD features from titles/descriptions. Separate source/target projections preserve direction; time-gap weighting and shrinkage can limit noisy rare transitions. Keep symmetric lexical similarity as a separate channel, avoiding automatic penalties for similar items. Fit next-item objectives using training histories; select channel weights by macro validation HR@10. Compatibility, substitution and redundancy remain latent hypotheses, never observed labels. No directly matching 2026 method was identified in this search.
